title: Organic Chemistry I & II
description: A rigorous two-semester, Year 2 sequence that develops organic structure, stereochemistry, mechanism, spectroscopy, and synthesis for chemical engineers. The course develops functional-group mastery while adding explicit reaction-energy reasoning, organometallic carbon–carbon bond formation, enolate chemistry, integrated retrosynthesis, modern analytical interpretation, polymer chemistry, green chemistry, and process-safety/scale-up judgment.

topics.title: Molecular Structure, Bonding, and Acid–Base Reasoning
topics.description: Establishes the electronic language used to predict structure, stability, physical properties, and reactivity.

children.title: Representing organic molecules
children.description: Fluent representations let students move from connectivity to geometry and reactivity without losing chemical information.

children.title: Lewis, condensed, line-angle, and three-dimensional structures
Formal charge, octets, lone pairs, and common valence patterns
Constitutional isomers and degrees of unsaturation
Bonding and electronic structure
children.description: Orbital models explain geometry, bond strength, polarity, and the availability of electrons for reaction.

children.title: Bond polarity, dipoles, and intermolecular forces
Resonance and acid–base reasoning
children.description: Resonance and pKa comparisons provide a general method for ranking stability and predicting equilibrium.

children.title: Valid resonance contributors and resonance hybrids
Inductive, resonance, orbital, and solvation effects

topics.title: Conformations and Stereochemistry
topics.description: Builds three-dimensional reasoning for molecular shape, chirality, selectivity, and structure–property relationships.

children.title: Conformational analysis
children.description: Conformations reveal how rotation and ring shape alter energy, accessibility, and product formation.

children.title: Anti, gauche, eclipsed, and steric interactions
Configuration and chirality
children.description: Configuration identifies stable three-dimensional arrangements that can produce distinct physical and biological behavior.

children.title: Enantiomers, diastereomers, meso compounds, and racemates
Stereochemistry in reactions
children.description: Students learn to translate a mechanism into stereospecific or stereoselective outcomes.

topics.title: Reaction Mechanisms, Energy, and Selectivity
topics.description: Replaces reaction memorization with electron-flow, kinetic, thermodynamic, and selectivity models that transfer to unfamiliar chemistry.

children.title: Electron-flow language
children.description: Curved-arrow mechanisms make bond breaking and bond formation explicit and testable.

children.title: Curved arrows for two-electron and radical processes
Intermediates, transition states, and catalytic cycles
Thermodynamics and kinetics
children.description: Energy diagrams distinguish whether a reaction is favorable from whether it is fast.

children.title: Free energy, enthalpy, entropy, and equilibrium
Selectivity and mechanism evaluation
children.description: A mechanistic hypothesis should explain observed rate, regioselectivity, stereochemistry, and competing products.

children.title: Carbocation, radical, carbanion, and concerted pathways

topics.title: Alkanes, Cycloalkanes, and Radical Chemistry
topics.description: Introduces hydrocarbon structure and conformational strain while developing the logic of radical chain processes.

children.title: Hydrocarbon structure and properties
children.description: Alkanes provide a clean setting for connecting structure, intermolecular forces, and bulk behavior.

children.title: Boiling point, melting point, solubility, and branching
Cycloalkanes and strain
children.description: Ring systems show how angle, torsional, and steric strain shape stability and reactivity.

children.title: Ring strain and heats of combustion
Fused, bridged, and spiro systems awareness
Radical reactions
children.description: Chain mechanisms introduce reactive intermediates important in halogenation, polymerization, oxidation, and process safety.

children.title: Inhibitors, oxygen sensitivity, and runaway awareness

topics.title: Alkenes and Alkynes: Structure, Synthesis, and Reactions
topics.description: Uses π bonds to connect mechanism, regiochemistry, stereochemistry, oxidation state, and polymer-forming reactivity.

children.title: π-Bond structure and preparation
children.description: Understanding π bonding explains restricted rotation, geometric isomerism, and electrophilic reactivity.

children.title: Addition mechanisms
children.description: A compact set of mechanistic patterns predicts connectivity and stereochemistry across many additions.

children.title: Catalytic hydrogenation and selective alkyne reduction
Oxidation, cleavage, and polymerization
children.description: Oxidative transformations diagnose or modify π bonds, while polymerization connects monomers to materials.

topics.title: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination
topics.description: Develops SN1, SN2, E1, and E2 as competing pathways governed by structure, solvent, nucleophile/base, temperature, and stereoelectronics.

children.title: SN2 and SN1 pathways
children.description: Substitution mechanisms connect molecular structure and medium to rate and stereochemical outcome.

children.title: E2 and E1 pathways
children.description: Elimination pathways explain alkene formation and the control of position and geometry.

children.title: Competition and synthesis
children.description: Students must choose among four pathways rather than apply each in isolation.

children.title: Product prediction and reagent selection maps

topics.title: Alcohols, Ethers, Epoxides, and Organosulfur Compounds
topics.description: Explores oxygen- and sulfur-containing compounds as solvents, intermediates, protecting groups, and industrial feedstocks.

children.title: Alcohol preparation and reactivity
children.description: Alcohols are central intermediates whose oxidation state and leaving-group behavior can be deliberately controlled.

children.title: Preparation by addition and carbonyl reduction
Acidity, hydrogen bonding, and physical properties
Conversion to halides, sulfonates, alkenes, and ethers
Ethers and epoxides
children.description: Ethers model relatively inert solvents, whereas strained epoxides enable selective ring-opening synthesis.

children.title: Sulfur analogues
children.description: Sulfur compounds broaden nucleophilicity and oxidation-state reasoning and appear in fuels, biology, and process streams.

children.title: Odor, toxicity, corrosion, and handling context

topics.title: Conjugation, Aromaticity, and Aromatic Reactions
topics.description: Explains delocalization and aromatic stabilization, then applies them to substitution, directing effects, and functionalization strategy.

children.title: Conjugated systems
children.description: Delocalized π systems explain unusual stability, color, and regioselectivity.

children.title: Aromaticity
children.description: Aromaticity is an electronic criterion, not merely the presence of a ring.

children.title: Aromatic substitution
children.description: Electrophilic and selected nucleophilic substitutions enable predictable ring functionalization.

children.title: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution and aryne awareness

topics.title: Spectroscopy and Integrated Structure Elucidation
topics.description: Combines IR, mass spectrometry, and one- and two-dimensional NMR evidence to determine structures and assess samples.

children.title: Formula, IR, and mass spectrometry
children.description: These methods rapidly constrain composition, functional groups, and plausible fragments.

children.title: Molecular formula and index of hydrogen deficiency
IR stretching regions and diagnostic bands
Molecular ion, isotope patterns, and accurate-mass awareness
NMR spectroscopy
children.description: NMR provides connectivity and environment information central to structure determination and reaction monitoring.

children.title: Integrated problem solving and analytical judgment
children.description: A defensible structure must satisfy all data and acknowledge ambiguity or impurities.

children.title: Mixtures, purity, solvent peaks, and common artifacts

topics.title: Organometallic Reagents and Carbon–Carbon Bond Formation
topics.description: Introduces powerful nucleophilic carbon reagents and selected catalytic couplings that expand synthetic design space.

children.title: Polarized carbon–metal bonds
children.description: Organometallic reagents reverse normal carbon polarity and create strong carbon nucleophiles.

children.title: Addition to aldehydes, ketones, esters, and carbon dioxide
Cuprates and related reagents
children.description: Softer organometallics expand substitution and conjugate-addition selectivity.

children.title: Catalytic coupling awareness
children.description: Selected cross-couplings illustrate how catalysis constructs C–C bonds at industrially useful selectivity.

children.title: Oxidative addition, transmetalation, and reductive elimination
Suzuki, Heck, and Sonogashira reaction recognition
Catalyst recovery, metals, cost, and waste considerations

topics.title: Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic Addition
topics.description: Treats the carbonyl as a polarized functional group whose additions control synthesis, equilibrium, and stereochemical outcomes.

children.title: Carbonyl structure and reactivity
children.description: Polarization makes the carbonyl carbon electrophilic and the oxygen basic, providing a unified reaction model.

children.title: Addition reactions
children.description: Nucleophile identity determines whether addition is reversible, followed by substitution, or paired with reduction.

children.title: Imine, oxime, hydrazone, and enamine formation
Oxidation, reduction, and selectivity
children.description: Carbonyl interconversions are central to synthesis and require deliberate chemoselective choices.

topics.title: Enols, Enolates, and α-Carbon Chemistry
topics.description: Develops carbon nucleophiles adjacent to carbonyls for alkylation, condensation, conjugate addition, and strategic bond construction.

children.title: Enolization and enolate formation
children.description: Acidity next to a carbonyl creates nucleophilic carbon centers with controllable position and geometry.

children.title: α-Functionalization
children.description: Enolates enable direct installation of carbon and heteroatom substituents next to carbonyls.

children.title: Condensation and conjugate addition
children.description: These reactions create efficient C–C bonds and recognizable retrosynthetic disconnections.

topics.title: Carboxylic Acids and Their Derivatives
topics.description: Unifies acyl substitution, derivative interconversion, hydrolysis, reduction, and process-relevant reactivity.

children.title: Acids: structure and preparation
children.description: Carboxylic acids combine resonance-stabilized acidity with distinctive physical and spectroscopic properties.

children.title: Preparation by oxidation, carboxylation, and nitrile hydrolysis
Nucleophilic acyl substitution
children.description: A common addition–elimination mechanism unifies derivative reactivity and interconversion.

children.title: Acid chlorides, anhydrides, esters, amides, and nitriles
Reduction, condensation, and process context
children.description: Acyl compounds are major industrial intermediates whose conversion and separation depend on equilibrium and selectivity.

children.title: Equilibrium conversion, water removal, corrosion, and waste

topics.title: Amines, Nitrogen Compounds, and Heterocycles
topics.description: Connects basicity, nucleophilicity, synthesis, and heterocyclic structure to pharmaceuticals, dyes, catalysts, and materials.

children.title: Amine structure and basicity
children.description: Lone-pair availability explains amine geometry, protonation, solubility, and nucleophilicity.

children.title: Synthesis and reactions
children.description: Multiple routes to C–N bonds must be compared for selectivity, overreaction, and functional-group compatibility.

children.title: Reduction of nitro, nitrile, amide, and imine groups
Heterocycles and applications
children.description: Nitrogen and oxygen heterocycles dominate pharmaceuticals, catalysts, dyes, and functional materials.

children.title: Pyridine-, pyrrole-, furan-, and thiophene-type aromaticity

topics.title: Integrated Synthesis and Retrosynthetic Analysis
topics.description: Integrates functional-group chemistry into multistep planning using selectivity, protecting groups, convergence, yield, safety, and evidence.

children.title: Retrosynthetic thinking
children.description: Working backward from a target turns a reaction list into a strategy for bond construction and functional-group placement.

children.title: Selectivity and sequence design
children.description: A viable route must manage incompatible groups, oxidation states, stereochemistry, and order of operations.

children.title: Route evaluation and proof
children.description: Chemical engineering demands routes that are not only plausible but also measurable, safe, scalable, and sustainable.

children.title: Atom economy, mass intensity, and solvent burden
Spectroscopic proof and decision-ready route comparison

topics.title: Biomolecules, Polymers, Green Chemistry, and Process Perspective
topics.description: Connects organic chemistry to biological molecules, polymer production, separations, hazard, sustainability, and scale-up decisions in chemical engineering.

children.title: Biomolecular organic chemistry
children.description: Biomolecules integrate stereochemistry, acid–base behavior, carbonyl chemistry, and noncovalent interactions.

children.title: Polymer chemistry
children.description: Polymer behavior emerges from monomer chemistry, mechanism, molecular weight, architecture, and processing history.

children.title: Degree of polymerization and molecular-weight distributions
Green chemistry, safety, and scale-up
children.description: Engineers must connect molecular transformations to material use, heat release, transport, separation, exposure, and end-of-life impact.

children.title: Twelve principles, atom economy, E-factor, and process mass intensity
Solvent/reagent selection and inherently safer design
SDS interpretation, incompatibilities, waste segregation, and exposure control
Mixing, heat transfer, gas evolution, runaway risk, and scale-dependent behavior
